# Porchlamp — Open-Source Contributor Value Index (https://porchlamp.org/)

> A porch lamp left on tells a visitor they are expected. Porchlamp ranks 11,000 open-source projects by what happens to a stranger's pull request, not by how many stars the project has. Every score traces back to recorded GitHub responses and SHA-256 content hashes (by Rahul Kumar, `pctablet505`).

## Core Empirical Findings (Snapshot `2026-10-17`, Benchmark `2.0.0-rc1`)
- **Dataset Scale:** 212,390 pull requests from 110,605 outside contributors tracked across 11,000 open-source repositories over six months across 6 ecosystems: `npm` (JavaScript/TypeScript), `pypi` (Python), `crates` (Rust), `go` (Go), `maven` (Java), and `systems` (C/C++/Zig).
- **More than 1 in 6 Active Projects Are Black Holes:** Of 4,042 licensed, maintained software projects that received at least 10 outside pull requests in six months, 720 (`17.8%`) left the majority of stranger pull requests with no human reply, review, or merge within 14 days.
- **More Stars, More Silence:** The black-hole rate increases with popularity: `16%` at 1k–10k stars, `19%` at 10k–50k stars, and `28%` at 50k+ stars (more than 1 in 4 of the most-starred repositories on GitHub).
- **Stars Barely Predict Contributor Experience:** Across all 4,181 ranked projects, the rank correlation between GitHub stars and the Porchlamp score is `0.08`, and only `9` of the 100 most-starred projects make the top 100.
- **Universe Breakdown (11,000 Total):**
  - `4,181` **Ranked (Rated)** under the default Balanced lens (`>=60%` parameter coverage and passing all Stage-0 gates).
  - `5,381` **Gated (Stage 0):** Black holes, archived, unmaintained, unlicensed, or non-software repositories (listed transparently under Not Ranked, never ranked).
  - `1,438` **Unrated:** Repositories passing Stage-0 gates but not ranked: `1,113` with `<60%` measured parameter coverage, `317` with no outside pull-request workflow, `8` that review off GitHub.
- **Coverage Tier Ceilings:** Repositories with `<95%` parameter coverage have their tier capped (`A (capped)` for `[80%, 95%)`, `B (capped)` for `[60%, 80%)`) so missing data never inflates a rank tier.

## One page per ranked project (readable without JavaScript)
To check a project, open https://porchlamp.org/projects/<owner>/<name>/ (lower case).
Each page opens with the project's median time to a first human reply to an outside pull request, the share that got no reply within 14 days, and its rank overall and for first-time contributors. Example: [ggml-org/llama.cpp](https://porchlamp.org/projects/ggml-org/llama.cpp/)

## Ecosystem and lens pages (readable without JavaScript)
Each page lists the top 50 projects of its cut, with score and tier, and each name opens that project's page.
- [Rust projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/rust/)
- [Python projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/python/)
- [JavaScript and TypeScript projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/javascript/)
- [Go projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/go/)
- [Java projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/java/)
- [C, C++ and Zig projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/c-cpp/)
- [Open-source projects for first-time contributors](https://porchlamp.org/first-timers/)
- [Open-source projects for building career capital](https://porchlamp.org/career/)
- [Open-source projects for senior systems engineers](https://porchlamp.org/senior-systems/)
- [Open-source projects for AI-assisted contributors](https://porchlamp.org/ai-assisted/)

## 5 Pillars & 18 Parameters (Balanced Weights)
1. **Responsiveness (25%):** Time to First Human Response (TTFHR), Decision Rate (90d), First-Timer Merge Rate, PR Ghost Rate (14d), and Time to Merge (p90).
2. **Criticality (25%):** Deduplicated Dependents, OpenSSF Criticality Score, and Monthly Registry Downloads.
3. **Governance (20%):** Legal IP Regime (OSI license & CLA/DCO), Elephant Factor, Promotion Ladder, and Bus Factor.
4. **Rigor (15%):** OpenSSF Scorecard Pipeline Defenses, AI Policy Posture, and Substantive Review Rate.
5. **Accessibility (15%):** Active Good First Issues, Newcomer Conversion, Newcomer Return Rate (90d), and Developer Experience.
